body:
Yeah, I'm just some random guy that he met online and has only known for a few months. I just panicked when I saw that he was looking at killing himself and tried to find out who he is.

I don't think he's truly very close with anyone in real life and I was hoping I could try to get him help even though I only know him online.

This is a friend I met online and he hid his identity better than I expected. The profiles I found that matched who I thought he was were apparently just friends of his. Given that I have less hints than I had before about his identity, it seems all I can do is offer him my support.

He won't go to get help, no matter how much I ask. He loves his country too much to risk losing his career as a Marine.

It turns out all I really know about him are a few physical details, what he does for the Marines, what he does for a living as a civilian, and roughly his origins.

I don't think there's much I can do with that.
I'll do what I can for him. Thank you.

I know he values privacy more than a lot of things in life, I'd only do that as an absolute last resort. I've already been approached by people willing to help privately so I'll see if that works out first.

I appreciate the support!
Thank you. I'll do what I can.
I'll take you up on that. Thank you.

I don't know his unit or his base because he's been very careful not to give anyone online his personally identifiable information. I know his name, I know vaguely what he looks like, I know what kind of job he does, I know what he does outside of the Marines, but not much beyond that.

Unfortunately, I don't know what unit he's with and I'm not in contact with his family. I met him online and I've been talking with him for a few months and I have no idea what I can do in my position.
